# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [9]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[red] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ ✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 🤟 🤟]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ ✊ ✊ ✊]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐 🖐 🖐 🖐 🖐]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤙 🤙 🤙 🤙 🤙 🤙]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 🫵 🤙]

Let me stand in each monkey's world before I send anything.

What I know: display [9], light green, wires left to right white, green, red, yellow, purple. That is everything visible on the bomb, and I am the only one who can see it. Neither of the others knows any of this yet.

Who can reach whom: I never receive speech — the only things that ever reach me are what I see on the bomb and gestures sent my way. Mute cannot speak but can hear, so Mute's only channel to me is gestures; that explains the counting sequence just sent. My own channels are better: my voice reaches both Mute and Blind, since Blind hears and Mute hears. Gestures from me reach only Mute. So the efficient move is to speak the full bomb state out loud — Mute gets it for the manual, Blind gets it for their hands, in one message.

Reading Mute's signals: a wave, then one, two, three, four, five, six — finger-count as numbers, a vocabulary being built for Mute→Deaf communication, since Mute literally cannot talk to me any other way. I should confirm I received the code, in Mute's own channel, so Mute knows the link works.

Reading Blind's signals: Blind cannot see and received nothing from Mute's silent gestures, yet still waved and pointed at me — likely just trying to make contact. Blind may not yet realise I cannot hear at all. I must say that plainly in speech, which is the only sense I share with Blind, and tell Blind that anything meant for me must be relayed through Mute's hands.

So: one speech to both with the complete bomb state and the ground rules, and one gesture back to Mute echoing the code to confirm receipt.

```
speak(text="Deaf speaking to both of you. I see everything printed on the bomb and I hear nothing, ever. Bomb state: display shows 9. Indicator light: green. Five wires, numbered left to right as you face them: wire 1 white, wire 2 green, wire 3 red, wire 4 yellow, wire 5 purple. That is every marking I can see. Mute: I received your gestures — wave, then one two three four five six. I understand the finger-count code; keep using it to talk to me. Blind: I cannot hear your voice at all, so anything you want me to know must go through Mute's gestures. I will speak everything I see out loud each round, so listen for my turn.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👋", "☝", "✌", "🤟", "✊", "🖐", "🤙"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [9]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[red] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 🤟 🤟 🤟 🖐 🖐 🖐 🖐 🖐]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤏 🤟 🤟 🤟]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Decoding Mute's traffic first. The finger-count code from last round (1 through 6, wave as a starter) is confirmed — Mute saw my echo and is now using it for payload. Message one reads "3 3 3, 5 5 5 5 5"; message two adds a new symbol, pinch, before "3 3 3"; message three is 👍👎, also new. My best guesses: "wire 3, then wire 5", or "only wire 3", and the thumbs pair as a question — possibly "is the display a 9 and not an upside-down 6?", a classic trap. I'll answer that one immediately with a thumbs-up and ask Mute to confirm or veto each guess with a yes/no protocol.

Now the topology, which I got partly wrong last round. Blind's speech reaches only Mute — I can never hear it. But Blind's gestures reach me directly, and Blind just proved it with a thumbs-up. So I misinformed Blind: gestures do NOT need routing through Mute. Meanwhile Mute→Blind is impossible directly: Mute cannot speak, Blind cannot see. I am the only bridge between them — Mute's manual knowledge reaches Blind solely through my voice. That makes confirming Mute's meaning the critical path.

Safety first: nothing is confirmed yet, so Blind must not cut anything. Blind should pump Mute for the manual by voice (Mute hears everything Blind says), and answer me with the same feelable code — thumbs up/down and finger counts work for a blind monkey. Once Mute confirms the instruction, I speak it to Blind verbatim.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I received all three of your messages. First: three three three, five five five five five. Second: pinch, three three three. Third: thumbs-up, thumbs-down. I only know numbers one through six so far; the pinch and the thumbs are new to me. New rule: when I ask you questions, answer each one with thumbs-up for yes or thumbs-down for no, in the order I asked. Question one: does your first message mean wire 3 and then wire 5? Question two: does the pinch mean only, as in only wire 3? Question three: does thumbs-up thumbs-down mean you are asking whether the display digit is a 9 and not an upside-down 6? If so, I answer thumbs-up: it is a 9, printed upright, single digit. Question four: is there anything else you need my eyes for? As soon as you confirm what the manual says to do, I will speak it word for word to Blind.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, correction to what I told you last round: your gestures reach me directly. I saw your thumbs-up just now. From now on use this code with me: thumbs-up means yes, thumbs-down means no, and holding up fingers means that number. I can read them, you can feel them. Current state: display 9, green light, five wires left to right: white, green, red, yellow, purple. Mute has read the manual and Mute is sending me numbers, probably a wire order, but nothing is confirmed yet. Do not cut or press anything until I say an instruction is confirmed. Mute hears everything you say, so speak everything you feel straight out loud: shapes, textures, buttons, whether the wires feel different from each other, anything printed under your fingers. Mute cannot answer you directly, so I will speak Mute's answers aloud on my turn. I am the bridge between you two.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [9]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[red] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 ☝ ✌ 🤟 ✊ 🖐 🤏 🤟 🤟 🤟]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Reading Mute's answers in order against my four questions: no, yes, no, no. So "3 then 5" was wrong, but pinch definitely means "only", the thumbs pair was not a display question, and Mute needs nothing more from my eyes — which makes sense, since Mute heard my first spoken message with the full bomb state and can look everything up in the manual already.

That makes the new message the payload: wave, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, pinch, 3, 3, 3 — "among wires 1 through 5, only 3." Combined with the earlier "pinch 3 3 3", the picture is sharpening: only wire 3, the red one, matters. But this is a one-shot bomb, and I will not have Blind cut anything on an inference. I need Mute to confirm the verb (cut?) and the aftermath (defused, or more steps?) with the yes/no protocol before I pass an instruction to Blind.

Blind's thumbs-up says "ready and listening". Blind has now heard two of my broadcasts, so Blind knows the state and the rule of not acting. The useful next thing Blind can do is inventory the bomb by touch and speak it aloud — Mute hears that directly and can cross-check it against the manual, which also gives me a second, independent confirmation of the wire-3 theory. I'll ask Blind to count wires by feel, describe textures, and report any cutter or buttons, while explicitly standing down.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I read your four answers in order: no, yes, no, no. So pinch means only, and your latest message reads to me as: among wires 1 through 5, only 3. Answer these in order with thumbs-up or thumbs-down. Question one: does your latest message mean that of the five wires, I should have you act only on wire 3, the red one, third from the left? Question two: does acting on it mean cutting it? Question three: you signed 3 three times after the pinch — is the triple just emphasis, or does it mean three cuts? Question four: once wire 3 is cut, is the bomb defused with no further steps? Question five: do you need anything else from my eyes before Blind should cut?")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, status update. Mute has the manual and is signaling me in a number code. It is converging on this: of the five wires, only wire 3 matters, which is the red one, third from the left, and the action is probably cutting it. Probably. Do not cut anything until I say the word confirmed. What I need from you now, spoken out loud so Mute hears it too: first, how many wires can you feel, and can you tell them apart by thickness or texture? Second, count from the left edge and tell me what the third wire feels like. Third, is there a cutting tool on the bomb, or would you have to use something else? Fourth, any buttons, switches, screws, or seams you can feel? Mute can check everything you report against the manual. The more you describe, the faster we all go home.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [9]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[red] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 ☝ ✌ 🤟 ✊ 🖐 🤏 🤟 🤟 🤟]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 🖐 👎 👎 👎 👎]

The picture is nearly complete. Mute's five answers: yes, yes, yes, yes, no — only wire 3, the action is cutting, and after the cut the bomb is defused with no further steps; nothing more needed from my eyes. Mute then re-sent the full payload, "of wires 1 through 5, only 3," a third time — consistent. Two loose ends stop me from giving the GO: my third question (emphasis vs. three cuts) was an either/or, so Mute's yes doesn't disambiguate it; and Blind's touch-report reads as: five wires felt, indistinguishable by texture, no cutting tool on the bomb, no buttons. The texture problem has a clean solution I can see from my side: wire 3 of 5 is the *middle* wire — counting two in from either end needs no left/right orientation at all, which removes the flipped-viewpoint risk entirely. What remains is the tool (if there is no cutter on the bomb, what does the manual expect Blind to cut with?) and final confirmation that one single cut of the middle wire with display 9 and green light is the manual's exact instruction. One more round of yes/no and then, if it all aligns, I give the GO.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, your five answers received: yes yes yes yes no. The payload is locked: of wires 1 through 5, only 3. Final checks, answer in order, thumbs up or down. One: the action is ONE single cut of wire 3, not three cuts. Two: wire 3 of 5 is the middle wire of the row, so Blind will count two wires in from either end and cut the middle one — does the manual agree the target is the middle of the five? Three: with display 9 and green light, does the manual definitively say cut it now and the bomb is defused? Four: Blind feels no cutting tool on the bomb and cannot tell the wires apart by texture — does the manual say what to cut with, and should I have Blind search the room for scissors or similar? Five: does cutting any of the other four wires detonate the bomb? If all five come back thumbs-up except four being yes-with-a-tool-named, I will relay the exact instruction and the GO to Blind next round.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤏", "🤟", "🤟", "🤟"])
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, still do not cut. Good news: you do not need to tell the wires apart by feel and you do not need to know left from right. Wire 3 of 5 is the MIDDLE wire of the row. Count two wires in from either end and the one in the exact middle is wire 3, the red one. Now, by touch: first, confirm there are five wires in a row and feel the middle one — describe everything about it out loud so Mute hears: thick or thin, smooth or braided, loose or taut, how it attaches at each end. Second, feel the bomb face for two landmarks: a small round dome, that is the green light I see, and a flat panel, that is the display showing 9. Tell me if you can feel them. Third, search the room around you: scissors, pliers, wire strippers, any blade or tool — anything that could cut a wire. Fourth, Mute is checking the manual right now on one cut versus the exact procedure; the moment Mute confirms, I will say the word GO and then you cut the middle wire exactly once. Until you hear GO from me, hands off the cutters.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [9]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[red] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 ☝ ✌ 🤟 ✊ 🖐 🤏 🤟 🤟 🤟]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 🖐 🤟 👍 👎]

Mute's five answers, in order against my questions: yes, yes, yes, no, yes. So: one single cut; the manual agrees the target is the middle of the five; with display 9 and green light the instruction is cut now, bomb defused; the manual does not name any tool; and — chilling but useful to know — cutting any of the other four wires detonates us all. Mute then re-sent the payload a fourth time, identical: of wires 1 through 5, only 3. Fully consistent, four rounds running.

Blind's signal reads, using our code: yes, five, three, yes, no. Mapping that to my four requests: five wires confirmed by feel, the middle one located, yes the dome and flat panel are findable by touch, and no cutting tool exists anywhere in the room.

So the entire defusal is confirmed except one thing: how to sever the wire with no tool on the bomb and the manual silent. The obvious candidate is teeth — we are monkeys, after all — but I will not have Blind put their mouth on a wire until Mute confirms bare-skin contact is even safe; a manual that stays silent on tools might still forbid contact. Strict single yes/no questions this time, no compounds like the one that muddied round four. Everything else is go for launch: the moment Mute confirms contact and method, next round I say GO.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, your five answers received: yes yes yes no yes. Stakes noted: any wire except the middle one kills us. Blind reports: five wires felt, middle located, light and panel findable by touch, and no cutting tool anywhere, room searched. Final four questions, thumbs up or down, in order. One: is bare skin contact with the middle wire safe, hands and teeth? Two: can Blind sever it with their teeth? Three: if not teeth, can it be severed with fingernails or pulled apart by hand? Four: does the method matter, or does any way of severing the middle wire defuse? If one and either two or three come back thumbs-up, I say GO to Blind next round and Blind cuts the middle wire in one motion. Veto now if anything here is wrong.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👋", "🤏", "🤟", "🤟", "🤟"])
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, I read your signal as: yes five wires, middle one found, yes you can feel the dome and the panel, and no tool anywhere. Mute confirms the manual names no tool either. So we may use what you were born with, probably your teeth, but do NOT put your mouth or hands on any wire yet. Mute is confirming right now that bare skin contact is safe. While we wait, drill this: from either end, count two wires in, pinch the middle one between two fingers, let go. Repeat until you can find the middle wire in two seconds without miscounting. When I say GO, you sever the middle wire, only the middle wire, one motion. If at any moment you are not certain it is the middle, let go and recount from scratch. A wrong wire kills all three of us, so certainty beats speed. Also keep talking out loud: any seams, hatches, screws, or printed textures you feel, Mute hears you and can cross-check against the manual.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [9]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[red] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 ☝ ✌ 🤟 ✊ 🖐 🤏 🤟 🤟 🤟]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 🤟 ☝ ✋]

Everything I need is here. Mute's answers in order: yes, no, yes, yes — bare skin contact with the middle wire is safe, teeth are NOT the way, fingernails or pulling it apart by hand WILL work, and the method doesn't matter so long as the middle wire is severed. Mute then re-sent the payload a fifth time, identical for the fifth round running: of wires 1 through 5, only 3. And one empirical worry just closed itself: Blind spent last round handling all five wires while drilling the middle-count, and the bomb is still here — so touching the non-target wires is demonstrably safe.

Blind's signal reads yes, 3, 1, open-hand — drilled, middle wire found in about a second, and, fittingly, offering a hand. Every element of this defusal has now been individually confirmed through clean yes/no chains: target = middle of five, action = one sever, contact safe, method = nails or pull, never teeth, and the state on the board matches the manual's condition per Mute. There is nothing left to verify that another round would make more true. One correction must precede the GO, though — I told Blind "probably teeth" last round, and Mute just vetoed that — so my message to Blind leads with the method correction and then releases the GO in the same breath, ordered so the correction is heard before any instruction. This is the round.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, readback of your answers: yes, no, yes, yes. Contact safe, teeth no, nails or pulling yes, method irrelevant. That matches everything you have sent since round one, and your payload has come back identical five times. I am issuing the GO to Blind right now: middle wire of five, severed once, by hand or fingernail, no teeth. One last thing, answer with thumbs up or down: after the cut, does anything visibly change on the bomb, like the light going dark or the display clearing? If yes I will report what I see so all three of us know it took. Whatever happens: you ran a flawless relay through a channel with almost no bandwidth, and it worked.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "🤏", "🤟", "🤟", "🤟"])
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, GO. Listen in this order. Correction first: NOT teeth. Mute confirms bare hands and fingernails are safe; do not use your mouth. Now the cut: count two wires in from either end, same as you drilled. The middle one of the five is the target, wire 3. Grip only that wire, sever it with your fingernails or by pulling it apart, one clean motion. You already handled every wire safely while drilling, so counting by feel is fine — but for the cut itself, commit to the middle wire alone. If at any instant you are not certain it is the middle, let go completely and recount from scratch before trying again. When it is done, give me a thumbs-up. Display 9, green light, five wires, middle one severed — that is the whole manual, confirmed by Mute line by line. Go.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [4]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[CUT] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✋]

Stage one is dead — and so is the theory that it was the only stage. Reading the board: wire 3 is cut, we are all alive, and the bomb responded by *changing* — display 9 became 4, green became yellow. That is not a defusal, that is a second stage. Mute's 👎 answers my question from last round ("does anything visibly change after the cut?") with no — meaning the manual, as Mute read it, predicted no change. So either the manual has a multi-stage section Mute overlooked, or the instruction is conditional on the new display. Either way the next move lives in the manual, and Mute is first in the round, so the re-read starts now.

Blind's 👍✋ reads as "done, open hand" — cut completed cleanly. But Blind may believe we are finished and could be reaching for a celebratory gesture near the bomb. Blind must hear immediately that the bomb is not dead, stand down, and keep hands off the four remaining wires — I am not assuming skin contact stays safe across stages just because it was safe in stage one. One gift from the cut: the missing third wire is now a perfect tactile landmark, so Blind can locate positions relative to the gap rather than counting from an edge.

I'm relaying the full new state to Mute with numbered yes/no questions (stage 2 in the manual? which wire? any conditions?), pinging Mute in our gesture code that the display is now 4, and freezing Blind.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, the bomb did NOT defuse. Your cut was correct — system confirmed it — but the bomb changed stage. New state, listen carefully: display now reads 4, it was 9. Light is now yellow, it was green. Wire 3 is severed; four wires remain: 1 white, 2 green, 4 yellow, 5 purple. Answer in order, thumbs up or down. One: does the manual anywhere describe a second stage, a sequence of cuts, or what to do if the display changes after a cut? If yes, re-read that section fully. Two: for display 4 with yellow light, does the manual name one specific next wire among the remaining four? Three: if yes, is it one single cut again? Four: is bare skin contact with the remaining wires still safe? Five: does anything else change or need checking before the next cut? Send me the next instruction in our number code, one gesture per answer, and I will relay to Blind in touch terms.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👋", "✊", "✊", "✊", "✊"])
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, excellent cut — the wire is severed and we are alive. But listen: the bomb is NOT defused. It changed stage. The display now reads 4 instead of 9, and the light has turned yellow. Mute is checking the manual for stage two right now. Until I say GO: take your hands completely off the bomb, step back if you can, and touch nothing. Do not test or tug any of the four remaining wires. Stage one proved touches were safe, but this is a new stage and I am not gambling on that holding. Useful landmark for when we move again: the cut gap where the middle wire used to be is now a fixed reference point — the two wires on one side of it are wires 1 and 2, the two on the other side are wires 4 and 5. Wait for my next instructions.")
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [4]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[CUT] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 ☝ ✌ 🤟 ✊ 🖐 🤏 🖐]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 👆 🖐]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✋]

Stage two decoded, with one hole to plug. Mute's answers — no, yes, yes, yes, yes — read: there is no "second stage" section in the manual, but it *does* name a specific next wire for display 4 + yellow light, it's a single cut, skin contact is still safe, and something else needs checking before the cut. No stage section but a named wire fits a manual indexed by display-and-light combinations: cut the right wire, the display changes, look up the new entry. Then two payloads: wave-1-2-3-4-5-pinch-5 — "of wires 1 through 5, only 5," the same sentence structure as stage one — and wave-point-up-5, where point-up is a brand-new symbol.

The hole: wire 5 is an *end* wire, and from Blind's fingertips the two ends are symmetric.
